name: Subpulmonary Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Hemodynamic Diagnostic Criteria for Subpulmonary Stenosis

criteria.description: Presence of a significant pressure gradient (>30 mmHg) across the right ventricular outflow tract on echocardiography
Evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy on imaging or electrocardiogram
Systolic ejection murmur best heard at the left upper sternal border
Hemodynamic confirmation of subpulmonary obstruction via cardiac catheterization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic pressure gradient >30 mmHg across the right ventricular outflow tract plus evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical examination and, if needed, cardiac catheterization.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur heard at upper left chest
systolic murmur at left upper sternum
ejection murmur at left upper chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right ventricular hypertrophy detected by echocardiography

searchTerms: palpable heart lift on right side
right ventricular heave felt on chest exam

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory abnormalities
imaging: Echocardiography showing subpulmonary obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy
Cardiac MRI for detailed right ventricular outflow tract anatomy
Chest X-ray showing right ventricular enlargement
genetic: May be associated with congenital heart disease syndromes; no specific gene identified for isolated subpulmonary stenosis
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and possible arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Obstruction at the pulmonary valve rather than subvalvular region
Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction with cyanosis

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as peripheral edema and hepatomegaly
Sudden onset of arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death
references: Maron BJ, et al. Clinical profile and management of subpulmonary stenosis. Circulation. 2020.
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease, 2022.
